summary.headline: Mallcom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR147 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 185 bps to 9.34% on raw material costs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR147 crore (+7% YoY), with EBITDA down 11% YoY to INR14 crore and margin at 9.34%, and PAT of INR6 crore (4.29% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR540 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR61 crore (11.21% margin, down 130 bps), and PAT INR30 crore; FY25 PAT included a one-time INR25 crore land-sale gain, so the years are not directly comparable. Export OEM realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and tariff-driven concessions, while the domestic business grew about 20%. Both new units (Sanand, Gujarat and Chandipur, West Bengal) are now commissioned and ramping up.

segments.name: Domestic (branded)
segments.commentary: Management says the domestic business grew about 20% YoY in FY26 and is the growth engine; branded business has better pricing power. Last month of Q4 was softer on cautious sentiment and gas shortages for some industries.

segments.name: Exports (OEM / white label)
segments.commentary: Realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and concessions to hold share. South America, Australia, Russia and Africa were described as doing well; Europe and US weak; Middle East okay. LatAm sales are white label.

segments.name: New products (PU coated gloves, PVC gumboots, nitrile)
segments.commentary: In-house manufacturing started as import substitutes; management says pricing is competitive with imports and margins are similar to company level. India PU glove imports estimated at INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Sanand, Gujarat (workwear/Protec unit)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; running at about 50% utilisation, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted from existing capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management says 10-12% revenue growth is the bare minimum for FY27 and it is confident of achieving it, with upside if conditions improve.
Management wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins over time, but said there are many ifs and buts at this stage; an analyst's 14-15% normalised margin framing was not explicitly confirmed.
Expects FY27 revenue growth to come more from domestic than exports.
Capex: INR34 crore spent in FY26; budget INR10-15 crore for FY27 and similar annual levels thereafter, covering maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur.
Expects to apply for a capital subsidy for Sanand, estimated at about INR10 crore under the state policy.
Expects debt, mainly working capital, to decline further and most debt to be repaid over about 4 years; finance cost could approach near zero in 3 years (analyst framing, CFO said 'possible').
capex_capacity: Sanand, Gujarat (Protec unit) has commenced commercial production; utilisation about 50%, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted.
Chandipur, West Bengal industrial safety shoe unit is fully operational; capitalised in FY26 with INR7 crore of subsidy received against INR14 crore machinery cost.
In-house manufacturing of PU coated gloves and PVC gumboots started.
FY26 capex about INR34 crore; FY27 budget INR10-15 crore, with ongoing annual spend in a similar range.
demand_pricing: Export OEM realisations fell in FY26 due to near-full-year prohibitive US tariffs, weak EU demand and concessions to retain share; price pass-through lags, especially in long-lead OEM business.
Input costs rose across textiles, leather, PU/PC/NBR polymers, driven by petro-linked prices, FX depreciation, freight and energy costs.
Domestic: price list revised twice in the last quarter; competitors also raised prices, and some stopped taking orders or cancelled open orders.

US: volumes fell, but management says this reflects tariff conditions, not product, quality or price. India is outside the US TAA list, so an FTA is seen as key to regaining share; order cycles run 3 months to 2-2.5 years.
Competition: China seen as better placed on raw material sourcing and currency; unorganised players expected to be hurt by the cost environment, which management sees as favouring organised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall, and which export product prices decreased?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower realisations were mainly in export OEM markets, due to weak demand and concessions to keep customers. Domestic price increases lag input cost rises.

qa_highlights.question: How much could 10-12% growth and a 14-15% normalised margin be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% growth is the bare minimum and it is confident of it. It wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins, which it describes as the profile it would like to maintain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and finance cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: no term loan; working capital debt is about flat YoY at INR110-115 crore. Expects further reduction and most debt repaid over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key domestic demand drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code formalisation, BIS standards tightening, rising worker awareness, wider distribution, more marketing and fleet, and import substitution. Management says domestic growth is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR34 crore; FY27 budget is INR10-15 crore, including maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur. Sanand subsidy of about INR10 crore is expected to be applied for this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market for PU gloves and PVC gumboots?
qa_highlights.answer: India imports an estimated INR80-90 crore of PU gloves; PVC gumboot market size was not quantified. Export revenue is also targeted for both products.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from petro-linked raw materials, FX and freight, with lagged pass-through to both domestic and export customers.
US market access: India is outside the TAA list, so recovery depends on a trade deal; EU demand and FTA timing also uncertain.
Sanand utilisation (about 50%) and ramp-up of new products against the INR40 crore revenue target.
Domestic demand softness in the last month of Q4 and possible cost-conservation by customers.
Subsidy receipt for Sanand (about INR10 crore) and debt reduction pace.
Q4 PAT margin of 4.29% and EBITDA margin of 9.34% as the base for FY27 margin recovery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the domestic business and on the 10-12% growth floor, but cautious on margins and export recovery. Management repeatedly said outcomes depend on raw material stability, trade deals and demand, and often answered with 'hopeful' or 'if things go well'.
key_quotes: 10%, 12% is the bare minimum we should be hitting, and we are confident of doing that for this year.
So, despite fresh investment, we could manage it internally.
We are just happy to not lose a customer.

growth.why: Management calls 10-12% FY27 revenue growth the bare minimum and is confident of it, backed partly by Sanand (INR40 crore minimum target at ~50% utilisation), new in-house glove/gumboot lines and domestic growth (~20% in FY26), though export realisations are weak and no order book figures were given.
